Outlet: CNBC, published Thursday November 5 2026 7:01 AM EST, updated 11:01 AM EST. By Chloe Taylor
Bank of England hikes interest rate for the first time since Iran war, warns inflation will near 5%

The Bank of England raised its key interest rate by 25 basis points to 4.0%, marking its first increase since August 2023. The Monetary Policy Committee voted 8-1 in favor, with the dissenting member supporting a 50 basis point hike to 4.25%.

U.K. inflation is now projected to reach "about 5%" by mid-2027, driven largely by energy price pressures stemming from the ongoing U.S.-Israel conflict with Iran, which began eight months ago.

Markets had priced in a 99% probability of a rate hike and a one-in-four chance of a December increase, according to LSEG data.
Yields: 10-year gilt yield 5.1546% (up 2 basis points); 2-year gilt yield 4.782% (up 4 basis points). The British pound remained flat against the dollar and euro.
September's annual inflation rate stood at 3.5%, driven by surging motor fuel costs.

Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey: "Without real progress towards settling the conflict in the Middle East... risks to energy prices, and so to inflation, are to the upside."
MPC member Catherine L. Mann voted for greater tightening, citing "non-linear inflation risks" and stating a 50-basis point hike in Bank Rate is "good policy."
